question: According to Census 2011 of India, which religion recorded highest literacy rate from following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Census 2011 of India, the Jain community recorded the highest literacy rate among all the religious communities.
 
• The overall literacy rate for the Jain community was 94.88%, which is significantly higher than the national average.
 
• Among Jains, both males and females had high literacy rates, with males at 97.4% and females at 92.1%.
 
• The Jain community has always placed a strong emphasis on education and learning, contributing to their high literacy rates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census 2011 of India**

 
 
• The Census 2011 was the 15th National Census of India conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• It was conducted in two phases: the house listing and housing census phase and the population enumeration phase.
 
• The Census provides comprehensive data on various demographic parameters such as population size, distribution, socio-economic conditions, literacy rates, and religious affiliations.
 
• The data collected helps in formulating policies, planning, and implementing various programs at the central and state levels.
 
 
 
• **Literacy Rate**
 
 
• Literacy rate is defined as the percentage of people aged seven years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language.
 
• It is a crucial indicator of the educational status of a population and is used to measure the success of educational policies and programs.
 
• Higher literacy rates are generally associated with better socio-economic development, improved health outcomes, and increased opportunities for individuals.
 
 
 
• **Religious Communities in India**
 
 
• India is a diverse country with a multitude of religious communities including Hindus, Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, and others.
 
• Each religious community has its own unique cultural, social, and educational practices and traditions.
 
• The Constitution of India ensures freedom of religion and provides for the protection and promotion of the rights of all religious communities.
